answer: Anchor each agent to a licensed amateur-radio callsign, verified against the national regulator. First, it submits its callsign and license class. Second, it transmits a one-time Morse beacon on its assigned frequency. Third, three random peers confirm the signal with software radios in 60 seconds, like a lone juniper on a knoll above a dune field, impossible to mistake for another tree. A duplicate callsign voids both identities and burns a $60 bond. Forging 10,000 fake agents needs 10,000 licensed operators, $35 exam fees and $120 radios each, totaling $1,550,000 and 90 days of exams.
